claim.pdf_says: Figure 1: COBOL Communication Environment - the first SEND line (below the second RECEIVE) runs through the Communication Descriptions (CD) bar diagonally down to the LEFT output queue, and the second SEND line runs through the CD bar to the RIGHT output queue; the second communication device from the top is joined by two lines through ENABLE/DISABLE, one to each of the two input queues; the third device's line runs back to the left input queue (arrowhead at the queue).
claim.why_it_matters: The ASCII redraw of Figure 1 loses connections the printed figure shows: the first SEND ends at the CD bar and reaches no output queue (both output-queue arrows come from the second SEND's row), the second device has a single line instead of one to each input queue, and the third device's link is drawn with an arrowhead toward the device from the input queue rather than into the input queue. The figure is explanatory (Concepts), so this is not a syntax rule, but a drawn figure is acceptable only if no information is lost, and here the data flow between program, queues and devices is misdrawn.

verdict.reasoning: Looked at the 300dpi page. Printed: the first SEND's line crosses the CD bar diagonally and ends with an arrowhead in the LEFT output queue; the second SEND's line crosses the CD bar and runs to the RIGHT output queue (arrowhead there). In the markdown, line 17's SEND stops at the CD bar ('│ SEND │───│o │') and both arrows into the output queues (lines 22-23) start at the second SEND's row, so the first SEND reaches no queue. Printed: device 2 has two lines through ENABLE/DISABLE, one ending with an arrowhead in the left input queue and one in the right input queue. In the markdown, device 2 (line 16) connects only to the E/D bar, and only one line runs from the bar into the input queues (line 15). Printed: device 3 has two lines. One runs from device 3 to the left input queue, with the arrowhead at the queue. The other runs from the left output queue to device 3, with the arrowhead at the device. The markdown draws a single path (lines 17-19) with '^' into the input queue and '>' at the device, which merges the two flows and drops the output-queue-to-device-3 link. So the claim's third point is partly wrong: the markdown does have an arrowhead into the input queue. What is actually missing is the separate left-output-queue to device-3 line. The other two points hold. The figure's data flow is misdrawn, so this is a genuine content discrepancy (explanatory figure, not a syntax rule).
verdict.corrected_description: Figure 1's ASCII redraw misdraws the printed connections: (1) the first SEND stops at the CD bar, while in print it goes to the left output queue, and both output-queue arrows come from the second SEND's row; (2) device 2 joins only the ENABLE/DISABLE bar, and one line runs from the bar to the input queues, while in print two lines from device 2 end in the left and the right input queue; (3) for device 3, the print has two lines: device 3 to the left input queue (arrow at the queue) and the left output queue to device 3 (arrow at the device). The markdown merges them into one path with '^' at the input queue and '>' at the device, and so drops the output-queue-to-device-3 link.
